children: Mumbai-based luxury catering services provider Foodlink F&B Holdings India, backed by Arpit Khandelwal of Plutus Wealth Management, has announced the price band for its initial public offering (IPO), which will open for subscription on November 26.
The company has fixed the price band at ₹181-₹191 per equity share. Investors can bid for a minimum of 78 shares and in multiples thereof.
At the upper end of the price band, the company aims to raise ₹360.76 crore through the IPO and is expected to command a post-listing market capitalisation of ₹1,190.9 crore.

The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth ₹192 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 88.35 lakh shares by the promoter and existing investors. The anchor book will open for a day on November 25, while the IPO will close on November 30.

Promoter Sanjay Manohar Vazirani and investors Arpit Khandelwal, V'Ocean Investments, Trans Global Hotels, Ankita Chugh, Aarkay Investments, Oaks Asset Management, Welspun Group Master Trust, through its trustee Balkrishan Goenka, Aarin Capital Partners and Bona Terra Greenhouses will offload shares through the OFS.

Foodlink F&B Holdings operates across three business segments: events catering; casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens; and banquets and integrated food and beverage (F&B) services. These segments contributed 44%, 30% and 25%, respectively, to the company's revenue during the six months ended September 2026.
The company plans to use ₹21.3 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue to set up a centralised kitchen and ₹41.5 crore to establish two new banquets.

It will invest another ₹50.8 crore in its subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants & Catering Services, to establish four new casual dining restaurants. Additionally, ₹21 crore will be used to repay debt, while the remaining proceeds will go towards general corporate purposes.

Promoted by Sanjay Manohar Vazirani, Foodlink F&B Holdings operates six centralised kitchens in India and one in Dubai, along with three banquets in India. It also runs 10 casual dining restaurants in India and seven in Dubai.
The company operates the JADE Luxury Banquets chain and casual dining brands such as India Bistro, China Bistro and Art of Dum.
As of September 2026, Foodlink F&B Holdings had total outstanding borrowings of ₹25.3 crore.
For the six months ended September 2026, the company reported a loss of ₹16.15 crore on revenue of ₹219.8 crore.
For the financial year ended March 2026, its profit rose 104.1% to ₹29.1 crore from ₹14.3 crore in the previous year. Revenue grew 25.9% to ₹567.5 crore from ₹450.9 crore over the same period.
Equirus Capital and JM Financial have been appointed as the merchant bankers to the IPO.
The company is expected to finalise the share allotment by December 1, with its shares likely to list on the stock exchanges on December 3.

title: Foodlink F&B Holdings announces IPO price band, aims to raise ₹361 crore
